claims.claim: In the Belgrade Lakes, sand made up about 20 % of the substrate at 0.5 m depth in front of undeveloped shores and 52 % in front of unbuffered developed ones
claims.location: p. 19 (PDF p. 19), Results 'Across Treatments'; Fig. 7; methods pp. 7–10
claims.quote: three times higher percentage of the substrate composed of sand (52%) than for REF (20%)
claims.conditions: visual estimates of percent cover of boulder, cobble, gravel, sand and silt along transects at 0.5 m and 1.0 m water depth in front of 8 properties per treatment on each of three lakes (East Pond, North Pond, Great Pond; 24 per treatment); REF = undeveloped reference shore with intact stratified vegetation and no structures; UD = developed, unbuffered (lawns to the shore); buffered developed (BD) sites had 17 %; Kruskal-Wallis H = 16.9, P = 0.006; no difference between treatments at 1.0 m
claims.note: The text does not say whether 52/20/17 % are means or medians (Fig. 7 plots medians and the tests are rank-based). The paper's 'preprint' label is right.

tried.note: bioRxiv rate limit on the OpenAlex link; the v1 full-text URL then worked

notes: Other results: percent cover of boulders, cobble, gravel and silt did not differ between treatments at either depth; embeddedness did not differ; sediment organic content was higher at REF sites but not significantly; substrate varied more between lakes than within (East Pond more boulders; East and North Pond more silt at 1.0 m; Great Pond more gravel at 0.5 m).
